dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Kevin.
Hi, Kevin. Is it all right if I ask something? I know it's Saturday afternoon, City Hall's closed, so I wasn't sure this was even the right number to call.
Yep, you got the right one. This line stays open outside regular hours for storm stuff. What's going on?

Okay, good. So it's the parking lot behind my building. I'm at 349 Chapel Street, up on the Hill. After that nor'easter that came in Friday and wrapped up today, the whole lot is running toward the back door. The water's sitting right at the threshold, and it came in a little.
Okay, 349 Chapel. Water pooling at the back entrance from the lot. Let me write that down. Is it coming in the door itself, or just pooling outside?

Both, kind of. It was pooling outside about two inches deep, and then it pushed under the door and wet the mat and the hallway floor. I put towels down. Is it all right if I ask if that's something you guys handle, or is it a building thing?
Fair question. If it's a drain in the lot, that depends on whose drain it is. Is there a catch basin back there, a grate you can see?
There's one grate, over by the dumpster. It's packed with leaves and who knows what. The lot slopes toward the door instead of toward the grate, honestly. That's what bugs me.
Gotcha. Grate by the dumpster, clogged with leaves, lot pitched toward the door. Writing all of it.
And my neighbor, he's been here a lot longer than me, he says it does this every big rain. Every single one. So it's not like this is news.
Yeah, that's helpful to know. A recurring thing goes in the notes differently than a one-off.
Can I ask you something else? Is that a city drain or a state one? Because somebody told me the state does some of the drains around here and I don't want to be chasing the wrong people.

Honestly, from here I can't tell you for sure. Drains on city streets are usually ours, state roads are the state's, and a drain inside a private lot might belong to the property owner. I'd have somebody look at it to sort that out. Is the lot part of your building, or is it shared?
It's behind the building, a few of us use it. I own my unit, so I guess it's the association's, but nobody on the board ever does anything. Is it all right if I ask what you'd do in my place?

Sure. I'd get this report in with us today so there's a record, and I'd tell your association in writing too, with a photo if you've got one. If it turns out the grate is tied into a city line, the crew can deal with it. If it's private, at least we'll have said so.
I have photos. I took about six on my phone, the water right at the door and the grate full of leaves.
Perfect. Keep those. Okay, let me get your name and a number so the crew or the office can call you back.
Tito Fortes. F-O-R-T-E-S. And the number's 401-555-0189.
Tito Fortes, 401-555-0189. Got it. Is that a cell?
Yes, it's my cell. I'm out in the car right now, so if it cuts out, that's why.
No problem. Now, is the water still rising, or has the rain stopped over there?
Rain's stopped. It's draining down a little, but slow. By tomorrow it'll probably be gone and then everybody forgets until the next storm. That's how it goes every time, I'm told.
Right. I'll flag it as a repeat drainage problem, and I'll note the leaf blockage so whoever checks it knows to look at the grate first.
Thank you. Is it all right if I ask how long before somebody comes out? I'm not asking for tonight. Just roughly.

After a storm like this the crews are stacked up with the bigger stuff, flooded streets, blocked drains on the roads. So I can't give you an hour. Likely early next week for someone to look. If it gets worse, or water starts coming further into the building, call this line right back.
Okay. That's fair, I guess. I just wish it got fixed once instead of reported every time.
Understood. That's why I'm putting the history in the notes.

One more thing, and this is separate, so tell me if I should call someone else. My neighbor's porch light, the one next door, has been flickering for weeks now. Is that you guys, or is that the electric company?
If it's a light on his own porch, that's his wiring or the utility, not us. If it were a city streetlight flickering, I'd take that. Is it a streetlight, or on his house?
On his house. Okay, then never mind, that's his business. I just figured with all the water around it might be a hazard.
It's worth him mentioning to the electric company if it keeps up, especially after a wet storm. Good that you thought of it.
Alright. So, to be clear, you've got the address, the lot draining to the back door, the clogged grate, and that it happens every big rain.
That's all of it. 349 Chapel, back lot, water at the back door, grate by the dumpster blocked, and a note that it's recurring. And I put in the question of whether it's city, state, or private.
Good. Thank you, Kevin. Is it all right if I call back Monday to check where it stands?
Absolutely. Call the main Public Works line Monday morning and give them your name and address.
Okay. Have a good rest of your Saturday.
You too, Tito. Stay dry.
